findings.breaking_input: A discover approval.requested event whose payload.gate is not a string, or whose cluster_tokens contains a token that is not a string but is filtered out, while another token is longer than 300 chars. The route calls `p.cluster_tokens.filter((t) => typeof t === "string")` then `.slice(0, MAX_TOKENS).map(text)` — text() applies clean() and slice(0, 300). But if a token is exactly 300 chars, it is served truncated without the "dropped" count reflecting it. More critically, an event whose payload.gate is not a string (e.g., an object) passes the `=== c.gate` gate check? No — `x.e.payload.gate === c.gate` with c.gate a string and payload.gate an object is false, so it is silently dropped, not counted in `dropped`. The route's `dropped` only counts winners over MAX_WINNERS, not winners dropped by gate mismatch, id grammar failure, or token over-length. So a winner with a malformed gate is invisible, violating "what a cap drops is counted, never silently cut".
findings.why: The comment claims caps report what they drop, but only the MAX_WINNERS cap contributes to `dropped`; winner-filtering by gate, idOf failures, and per-token truncation are not counted. A wrong-shaped gate (object) is a malformed event that is skipped without any accounting, the exact "A malformed id dropped silently" / "A wrong-shaped source returned an empty inventory" class.
findings.fix: Count every skipped candidate entry — non-string gate, id outside ULID, over-limit token truncations — in `dropped` and report per-reason; refuse a non-string gate as a named finding.
findings.twin_of: A malformed id dropped silently -> malformed input is a named finding, never an omission.

findings.breaking_input: A discover event where the envelope `process` is the discover prefix but the entry's `id` is a 26-char string with a lowercase letter or the digit '0' or '1', which ULID excludes. `idOf` returns "" → `ofDiscover(e) && idOf(e.id) === ""` → dropped++ and the entry is counted as dropped. But the same entry ALSO fails the filter's `ok` (since isPlain(e) and typeof e.kind are true, it passes ok; the entry is dropped once). However, if the same id appears in `decision.recorded`'s payload.decides and also in an approval.requested's envelope id, the decisionOf map keys by `idOf(x.e.payload.decides)` — if that decides id is malformed (lowercase), idOf returns "" and `decides !== ""` is false, so the decision is never attached to the winner it decides, leaving the winner 'open' forever even after a real decision. The route then serves `state: "open"` and `decision: null` despite a decision.recorded existing — the "A decision anyone could write" / "validate one read, compare another" class: the winner's state reads one attribute (its own id) while the decision's join reads a different one (payload.decides).
findings.why: A malformed decides id (e.g. from a hand-typed or truncated receipt) is silently ignored by the state join, showing a winner as undecided when a decision exists — a wrong "open" that invites a user to decide again, and the spine refuses a second decision, so the state is permanently wrong.
findings.fix: Require decides to match the ULID grammar and the decision to join against a winner whose id is also valid; report a malformed decides as a named unresolvable, never a silent 'open'.
findings.twin_of: Two readers of one fact share one predicate.

findings.breaking_input: A discover approval.requested with `cluster_tokens` as a sparse array (e.g., `[,"invoice",]`) — `Array.isArray(p.cluster_tokens)` is true, filter keeps "invoice", fine. Or an array with `null` inside — filter drops null fine. But an array with a token that is a Number (e.g., 42) — filtered out, not served, fine. The hole: a token string that is itself a 26-char ULID-looking value, or a token string containing a newline, is served into the fold, which joins tokens with ", " into a single cell; a token containing a newline, combined with the "one-line" rule (every free text bound for a parsed log is one line), would break the serving table on the rendered page — the fold's `tokens.join(", ")` produces a cell with an embedded newline, violating the room's own one-line contract and the "ids are grammar-checked" rule for anything that looks like an id.
findings.why: cluster_tokens are free text that goes straight through text() with no newline scrubbing; the fold joins them raw into a table cell. A token that is an id-like string or carries a CR/LF corrupts the cell's line-oriented rendering, and the route's "one line" guarantee is not upheld.
findings.fix: Scrub cluster_tokens through the same line rule the fold's cells use (replace control chars), and apply the ULID grammar check to any token that looks like an id.
findings.twin_of: Every free text bound for a parsed log is one line (JSON-escaped); the ids-are-grammar-checked twin.

findings.breaking_input: Two approval.requested events with the SAME id (e.g., a replay or a torn append that duplicated a line). `decisionOf` maps `idOf(x.e.id)` to the decision, but the winners list iterates `all` (all approval.requested) and would serve BOTH entries with the same id, producing two rows with the same key in the React table — a duplicate React key, the "A name the registry listed twice was counted twice and drawn under a duplicate React key" class. `decisionOf.get(x.e.id)` would resolve both to the same decision, but the table still draws two identical rows.
findings.why: No dedup of winners by id; duplicate receipts (which the spine might hold if a torn line was re-appended) draw duplicate rows with a duplicate key, and the "dropped" count never reflects it.
findings.fix: Dedup winners by id (keep the oldest), count duplicates dropped, and pin with a mutant that duplicates a winner.
findings.twin_of: A name the registry listed twice was counted twice and drawn under a duplicate React key.

findings.breaking_input: An event that is not plain (e.g., a JSON line that parsed to an array, a string, or null) — `isPlain` returns false, `ok` false, the filter returns false and the entry is silently skipped, never counted in `dropped`. The comment says "an entry whose id is not one is skipped and COUNTED", but a non-object event is skipped without any count. The spine could hold a torn line (a JSON array), and the availability would still be "served" with the torn line invisible.
findings.why: Non-object events are dropped without accounting, so a torn spine line is invisible rather than a named finding — violating the spine's own "a JSON line that is not an object is torn" rule and the route's promise that skipped entries are counted.
findings.fix: Count non-object events in `dropped` (or better, report them as torn/unreadable and flip availability to unknown, matching the sane corruption class).
findings.twin_of: A spine line that parses to a non-object (`null`) was kept as an event -> a JSON line that is not an object is torn, in every engine.

findings.breaking_input: A `run.completed` event where `x.e.payload.step` is the string "hunt" but the event has NO `payload.outcome` and no `e.outcome` (e.g., a malformed writer). `run()` returns `outcome: text(r.e.payload.outcome) || text(r.e.outcome)` → both empty string → `outcome: ""`. The route returns `outcome: ""`, and the fold's `runSub` prints `outcome ${field(run, "outcome") || "unstated"}` — that's fine. But the run's `id` is via `idOf(r.e.id)` — if malformed, id is "", and the fold's `runSub` does `field(run, "id").slice(-6)` on empty string → "". The KPI still shows `day` and the run exists, so `any` counts it. A run whose id is malformed and whose day is unreadable (day text of empty) is still served as a run with empty fields, not counted as dropped — a malformed run is silently served rather than named.
findings.why: Malformed run.completed events (bad id, missing day) are served as runs with empty strings rather than skipped and counted; the "every envelope id and ts is served only in its grammar" rule is broken for runs (only winners check idOf).
findings.fix: Skip a run whose id fails the ULID grammar and count it; require day to be a real date string.
findings.twin_of: Envelope fields passed through unvalidated -> every envelope id and ts is served only in its grammar (`idOf`, `tsOf`).

findings.breaking_input: `discoverConstants` validates `PROCESS` with `m.PROCESS.indexOf("@") < 1`, so a PROCESS like "@" (index 0) is rejected, but "x@" (index 1) passes (slice(0,2) = "x@") and a process "yo@" passes as prefix "yo@". Now `ofDiscover` uses `e.process.startsWith(c.prefix)` — any process whose name STARTS with "yo@" is treated as discover, even "yo@evil" from a face actor that wrote a process string "yo@evil". The prefix is not anchored by the version grammar, so a second actor can forge a discover process by naming its process "yo@anything". The comment says "any version of discover is discover", but "any name ending with @" is not discover. A face or another tool can emit `idea.captured` with process "yo@fake" and it will be counted as a discover capture.
findings.why: The prefix check `slice(0, indexOf("@") + 1)` accepts any process whose name before '@' matches, with no grammar on the name segment (e.g., must be [a-z0-9-]+), so a spoofed process name is indistinguishable from discover's, counted as a discover receipt.
findings.fix: Validate the PROCESS name against a grammar (e.g. /^[a-z0-9-]+@/), and require the full process to match a stricter pattern (name@semver), not just a prefix on the name.
findings.twin_of: An id trusted as a key -> A key the client links by exists only for an id with a contained `<dir>/<id>.md` page.

findings.breaking_input: A discover `approval.requested` whose `payload.slug` is empty and `payload.niche` empty, but score is a number — served as a winner row. The fold's `servedTable` row returns `field(w, "id") === "" ? null` — so if id is empty, row is null (counted? no, `dropped` doesn't count it). But if id is a valid ULID yet slug and niche are empty, the row is served with blank cells. The route has no rule requiring a winner to carry a slug; an approval.requested with no slug is a malformed winner that is still served, and the "empty value read as an absent one" class.
findings.why: No shape validation on a winner's required fields (slug, niche, score presence); a winner without a slug is served as a real venture, inviting the user to approve something un-named.
findings.fix: Require slug to be a non-empty string and count a winner that fails as dropped; name it.
findings.twin_of: A value checked for presence, not validity -> a port is decimal digits in 1..65535.

findings.breaking_input: `discoverConstants` accepts `m.PROCESS` and `m.WINNER_GATE` from the file, but never checks that `WINNER_GATE` is a plausible gate shape (e.g., it could be ""+a newline, or a string with a control character). If WINNER_GATE is "ev\n", then `x.e.payload.gate === c.gate` with c.gate containing a newline matches an event whose gate also has that newline; a forged event with a gate "ev\n" would look discover-authentic. The gate is a free string with no grammar, so a second spelling (leading/trailing whitespace) can sneak past the "exact string" check that is supposed to prevent a second grammar — a case-folded or whitespace variant is a different string, but the route treats any string equal to the file's as the gate, so a gate with an invisible character is a second grammar.
findings.why: The gate is not validated to be a sane token (e.g., /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/), so a gate carrying whitespace or control characters is a distinct gate a malicious actor can also use, defeating the "no second grammar" promise.
findings.fix: Require WINNER_GATE to match a strict token grammar; refuse a gate with whitespace/control.
findings.twin_of: A misspelt `levels:` drew a ladder with no rung.

findings.breaking_input: `discoverBody` takes `c.prefix` as "name@" and checks `process.startsWith(prefix)`. A process exactly "name@" (with empty version) passes startsWith. The comment claims "any version of discover is discover" but an empty version is not a version; a tool that emits process "name@" with no version is counted as discover even though the spine's own writer would require "name@x.y.z". A face tool or a hand-edited receipt with process "name@" is counted as a discover capture.
findings.why: The prefix check with no requirement for a populated version allows an empty-version process to be attributed to discover.
findings.fix: Require the segment after '@' to be a non-empty version string (e.g. /^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/).
findings.twin_of: An unknown outcome read as "not raised" -> a guard's release condition is "certainly did not happen", never "did not see it happen".
